The value is sourced from acoustic measurement of a stone cavity, not derivation.

holes_found.description: Cross-WIN numerical inconsistency on Tesla base frequency. detail_evidence and detail_extra both state '10 × 11.7 Hz (Tesla, WIN-001) = 117 Hz' but WIN-001's canonical value is 11.78 Hz (data/wins.json:001 claim 'Tesla 11.78 Hz resonance,' finding text 'converts to ~11.78 Hz'). Using the WIN-001 value, 10 × 11.78 = 117.80 Hz, off from the 117 Hz observation by 0.7%. This is not a substantive flaw — the rebuttal argument is mechanism-based (no EM↔acoustic coupling), not arithmetic-based, so the precision doesn't change the conclusion. But a careful defender quoting both WINs side-by-side could note 'your own review uses two different Tesla numbers.' Cosmetic at most. Could be fixed by a 2-character edit (11.7 → 11.78) in both detail_evidence and detail_extra. NOT a blocker for closing qid=451 — this finding pre-dates the c4 patches and was not introduced by them.
holes_found.recommendation: Minor edit: in detail_evidence and detail_extra, change '10 × 11.7 Hz (Tesla, WIN-001) = 117 Hz' to '10 × 11.78 Hz (Tesla, WIN-001) = 117.8 Hz' for cross-WIN consistency with WIN-001. Optional; can be batched with any other minor edits to WIN-003 rather than triggering its own patch run.

stronger_arguments.description: No new stronger arguments emerged this cycle. c4's textbook citation suggestion (Kinsler et al., Fundamentals of Acoustics ch. 9) was not picked up by the decider's patch and remains an outstanding could-strengthen — but it is not a hole, just a possible enhancement. Re-flagging once: anchoring the v_air/(2L)=75.6 Hz computation to a textbook makes the physics calculation harder to challenge as 'just curmudgeon opinion.'
sources: Kinsler, Frey, Coppens, Sanders — Fundamentals of Acoustics, 4th ed., ch. 9 (cavity resonance)

kernel_of_truth.description: The 117 Hz acoustic measurement is real and the c4 patch now correctly identifies the resonating medium (data/wins.json:003 detail_evidence: 'the speed of sound in the enclosed air (~343 m/s) — an air-cavity standing-wave mode bounded by the rigid granite walls'). The chamber is genuinely acoustically interesting — air-cavity standing waves in granite-walled enclosures are studied in architectural acoustics for concert halls and historical reconstructions.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The dome's interpretation is still unsupported even after the (correct) air-cavity acknowledgment. data/wins.json:003 detail_evidence still notes 'zero mechanism for electromagnetic dome fields to drive acoustic vibrations in stone' — and the harmonic-of-dome-resonance framing has (i) no specified base frequency derivable from dome geometry yielding 117 Hz, (ii) no coupling mechanism between EM dome modes and mechanical air-cavity resonance, and (iii) free post-hoc selection across multiple integer-multiple matches (10×11.78, 15×7.83). Fixing the granite/air physics error removed a credibility-undermining footnote (per c4 advocate-mode tu-quoque defense) but did not strengthen the dome's positive case.

advocate_mode.best_defense: With the granite/air physics error fixed, the c4 tu-quoque defense (strength 4) collapses to strength 1: 'Your debunk now correctly identifies air as the resonating medium, but you still ignore the dome model's claim that the firmament cavity provides the underlying EM field structure that excites resonance in any cavity, not just this one.' This is a much weaker move — it asserts a mechanism (firmament EM excites mechanical cavities) without specifying how, what frequency couplings, or why all stone chambers don't resonate identically. The dome offers no formula here.
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: No urgent action needed. The c4 tu-quoque is neutralized. If a future dome-side update articulates a specific EM-to-mechanical coupling proposal for firmament-driven cavity excitation, re-engage at that point. For now, this WIN is stable.

deeper_analysis: qid=451 verification: clean closure. The decider's c4-derived patch implemented H1's recommendation essentially verbatim (data/wins.json:003 detail_evidence:1 in commit 1c903d7), and H2 (the ISS-2366 mis-framing) was resolved structurally — first by rewriting ISS-2366's title and description to capture the actual physics error (now visible in closed-issues.json:ISS-2366 record), then by closing ISS-2366 once EXP-530 confirmed the patch had landed (closure-ledger.jsonl:2026-06-02T01:13). The closure-ledger entry transparently states 'EXP-530 fix already applied to wins.json in commit 1c903d7 (prior decider run). Air-cavity correction confirmed in current HEAD.' This is the right outcome for c4 H2: the routing failure was corrected and the underlying physics error was fixed in the same window. The Tesla 11.7 vs 11.78 cross-WIN inconsistency (holes_found[0]) is a pre-existing cosmetic issue that was present in c1 through c4 and not introduced by the qid=451 patch — flagging it now because cross-WIN consistency is one of the expanded review lenses, but it does NOT block closure of the qid=451 verification cycle. Recommend no_change as the gating decision for qid=451; the cosmetic 11.7→11.78 fix can be batched with future minor edits.
